synopsis: A rain-wet evening commute drops below the city and keeps descending until the window opens onto an endless vertical furnace city.

shots.prompt:
HOOK. Open already mid-motion on one ordinary object passing the glass at arm's length, so close and so fast it is only a streak. A dull, grey, utterly routine commute. At 1.5 seconds a two-note chime cuts in and a calm neutral announcer says the destination line. Nobody reacts and nothing changes. The train immediately accelerates hard. By 6 seconds ONE thing far ahead is unmistakably wrong, and it is already growing.

Rain-wet industrial outskirts in flat grey evening light. A rust-dark gantry leg whips past the glass close enough to blur, then a signal post, then a line of freight wagons stripping past at arm's length. The announcer says exactly: "Next stop: Hell." Nobody reacts. The train slams into acceleration. By 6 seconds the track ahead has begun to tilt downward and the sky above the far horizon burns dull orange.

HARD BREACH. In the first half second something enormous slams past the glass at arm's length and blacks the frame out for an instant. Coming out of that darkness the ordinary world is already gone and the line has physically committed to the destination with no way back. The shot ends with the destination's first true landmark resolving far ahead.

The carriage judders hard as a concrete tunnel portal slams past the glass and blacks the frame. The line is now pitching steeply DOWN and the carriage noses forward with it. Out of the darkness the train runs on a ledge bolted to the wall of a vertical shaft with no bottom, steel stanchions whipping past one every fraction of a second. Orange light rises from far below, the pressure builds and the pane ticks with heat stress.

ARRIVAL EDGE. Open on a violent change of light in the first half second: the exposure blows out white or crushes to black and recovers. Then the first landmark grows continuously across the whole shot until it no longer fits inside the window. Show how far down or how far up the place goes. The scale must be frightening.

A violent jolt shakes the camera and the exposure blows out orange. The descent has steepened until the track is falling away beneath the window. The shaft wall ends on a cavern with no far wall: black basalt canyons drop kilometres further below the track, molten rivers run white-hot along the floor, and embers rip upward past the glass. Far across the void, foundry towers taller than the cavern already stand, growing.

FLYTHROUGH. Open with that landmark's mass already passing the window at close range, filling the glass and strobing the interior. Maximum parallax: foreground elements cross the frame in a fraction of a second while the true size of the place is revealed by what lies beyond them. Something larger still is already visible ahead.

The carriage judders and heat hits the glass. The train has dropped to the level of the foundry wall and runs its full length at arm's length: black basalt piers cross the glass one every fraction of a second, and between them furnace mouths flood the carriage with light so hot the interior goes black by contrast. There is no sky, only black rock roof lost in smoke overhead, and every trace of light comes from the molten metal below.

DEEPEST SCALE. Open with a hard impact against the glass in the first half second - heat, pressure, spray or a shockwave that jolts the camera and knocks the focus. Then the widest and deepest view of the destination so far, too large for the window to contain. The single most spectacular second of the episode belongs here.

A pressure wave slams the glass, the whole carriage shakes and the focus hunts. Chains as thick as the carriage swing past and black out the view. Between them the camera looks straight DOWN, still descending, into an abyss lined with molten terraces stacked level below level below level past resolution. Above the abyss the air is lightless black with no horizon and no cloud; all light rises from far beneath the window.

HEART AND PAYOFF. Open with the train passing through or beneath something colossal. Travel alone carries it into the centre of the place. At about 8.5 seconds a calm ordinary commuter announcer quietly says the arrival line. Then the chime sounds again, the same voice begins only "Next stop-" and the shot ends mid-word while the train is still moving forward and something new is already growing ahead.

A last hard jolt and the train passes beneath a span so vast its glowing underside fills the entire window. Out the far side the descent finally levels out at the floor of the world: molten arteries running between black terraces to the horizon, enormous unmoving silhouettes on distant platforms, nothing the size or shape of a person. Overhead is solid black, the darkest frame of the journey. The announcer says exactly: "Welcome to Hell."
